place.zh: 石坳村 · 家中 · 天未亮

setup.zh: 立冬这天，天还没亮。娘卸下一条鹿腿，塞进一只小腌菜坛子，往你怀里一塞：「给吴婆婆送一坛腌菜去。走屋后头，趁天没亮。」
setup.en: The Start of Winter, before dawn. Your mother takes off one leg of the deer, stuffs it into a small pickle jar and pushes the jar into your arms: "Take Granny Wu a jar of pickles. Go round the back. Before it's light."

recap.zh: 立冬天没亮，你抱着一坛「腌菜」躲过马家的家丁，给吴婆婆送去了鹿腿。她讲了一个故事：一口鼎，一条龙，一张掉下来的弓——鼎湖，乌号。然后她朝你肩上看不见的银光，慢慢低下了头。
recap.en: Before dawn on the Start of Winter you carried a jar of "pickles" past the Mas' men and brought Granny Wu the leg of venison. She told a story: a *ding*, a dragon, a bow that fell — Dinghu, Wuhao. Then she slowly bowed her head toward the silver on your shoulder she could not see.

zh: 一只腌菜坛子，芥菜底下压着一条鹿腿。
「早年间，有一个皇帝……铸了一口鼎。」
她朝着那团看不见的银光，低下了头。
en: A pickle jar; under the mustard greens, a leg of venison.
"Long ago there was an emperor… he cast a *ding*."
She bows her head toward a silver light she cannot see.

story.zh:
立冬这天，是九月十五。天还没亮，小满是给他娘剁骨头的声音吵醒的。

「咚。咚。咚。」一声一声，又沉又稳。他爬起来往灶间一看，只见他娘挽着袖子，拿他爹那把剥皮的短刀，顺着骨缝一刀一刀地走，走到关节那里，手腕一翻，「喀」的一声，一整条鹿后腿便卸了下来。他爹蹲在一旁看着，张着嘴，看了半天，道：「……你什么时候学的？」他娘道：「看你剥了十几年兔子。」

她到炕头打开那只木箱，翻出一块包腿的布来。翻的时候，她把箱底一个巴掌大的旧布包拿起来，搁在一边；找着了布，又把那个布包放回了原处，放得很轻，轻得像放一个睡着了的孩子。小满知道那布包里包的是什么，那是那只碗的七八片。

她在膝弯那里又下了一刀，把鹿腿斩作两截，拿布包了，揭开墙角那只腌芥菜疙瘩的缸，把两截鹿腿埋进芥菜底下，一层一层压实了，盖上木盖。小满道：「娘，鹿腿也能腌？」他娘道：「能。」小满道：「好吃吗？」他娘道：「不知道。没腌过。」说着拿草绳把那只缸捆了，往他背上一绑，道：「给吴婆婆送一缸腌菜去。走屋后头，别走井台。趁天没亮。」

小满背着缸，一肚子的不明白。他娘却已把剩下的肉、皮、角、下水，都在院子里摊开了，摊得整整齐齐，像是摆摊，那一挂下水，偏偏摆在最当门的地方。然后她洗了手，把袖子放下来，坐在门槛里头，等着。
story.en:
The Start of Winter fell on the fifteenth of the ninth month that year. Before it was light, Xiaoman was woken by the sound of his mother chopping bone.

*Thok. Thok. Thok.* One stroke after another, heavy and steady. He got up and looked into the kitchen: his mother, sleeves rolled, his father's skinning knife in her hand, was working along the seam of the bone stroke by stroke; at the joint she turned her wrist — *crack* — and a whole hind leg of the deer came away. His father crouched to one side watching, mouth open, a long while. "…When did you learn that?" His mother said, "Watching you skin rabbits for ten-odd years."

She opened the wooden chest at the head of the kang and dug out a cloth to wrap the leg. As she searched, she lifted a small old cloth bundle, the size of a palm, from the bottom of the chest and set it aside; when she had found the cloth she put the bundle back where it had been, very gently, as gently as laying down a sleeping child. Xiaoman knew what was wrapped in it: the seven or eight pieces of that bowl.

She cut once more, at the hock, so the leg came apart in two pieces, wrapped them in the cloth, took the lid off the mustard-tuber crock in the corner, buried the two pieces under the greens, pressed them down layer by layer, and put the lid on. Xiaoman said, "Ma, can you pickle a deer leg?" His mother said, "You can." Xiaoman said, "Is it good?" His mother said, "Don't know. Never pickled one." And she roped the crock and tied it onto his back. "Take Granny Wu a crock of pickles. Go round the back of the houses, not by the well. Before it gets light."

Xiaoman stood with the crock on his back and a bellyful of not understanding. His mother had already laid out the rest — meat, hide, antlers, offal — all over the yard, neat and orderly, like a market stall, and the offal she set right in front of the door. Then she washed her hands, let down her sleeves, sat down just inside the threshold, and waited.

story.zh:
村东头那户，吴婆婆已经坐在门槛上了，脸朝着东边，那里刚刚透出一线鱼肚白，她晒的大约是这一线白。

小满走到她跟前，还没开口，她已道：「鹿腿来了？」

小满背着缸，愣住了。他娘一个字也没提鹿腿。他道：「……您怎么知道是鹿腿？」

吴婆婆道：「你爹答应的。在山涧边上，蹲着摸那个蹄印的时候。」

小满心里「咯噔」一下。那山涧在黑松岭里头，离这门槛少说也有三四十里地。他道：「婆婆，您又不在山涧边上。」

吴婆婆笑了，露出那三颗牙来：「我耳朵好。」

她揭开缸盖闻了闻，道：「你娘是个聪明人。」说着拍了拍门槛：「坐。」

小满便坐下了。吴婆婆问道：「你爷爷那张弓，昨儿拉开了？」小满一愣：「……拉开了。」吴婆婆点了点头，仰着脸，朝着东边那一线白，慢慢地讲了一个故事。

早年间，天底下头一个皇帝，采了山上的铜，在一座山底下铸了一口鼎。鼎成那天，天上下来一条龙，垂下胡须来接他。皇帝骑上去了，大官、娘娘跟着爬上去七十几个，龙便往天上飞。

剩下些小官儿，挤不上去。有一个小官儿，家就在那山脚底下，有个闺女，才七八岁。他扑上去抓住了龙须，吊在半空里，底下他闺女仰着脸，一声一声地喊他。龙须扯断了，人都掉了下来，跟着掉下来的，还有那皇帝的一张弓。

小满道：「那闺女呢？」吴婆婆道：「……哭呗。」

她停了一停，又道：「老百姓仰着头，抱着那张弓哭。后来的人，管那地方叫鼎湖，管那张弓，叫乌号。上去的上去了，留下的，就守着一张弓。」

小满问道：「那张弓，后来有人拉开过吗？」

吴婆婆转过脸来，朝着他，慢慢地露出一个笑来：「你问得好。」

便不再往下说了，只自言自语地添了一句：「修仙修仙，修成个想上天的人，也就修到头了。」

说完了，她伸出那只枯瘦的手来摸他的头，摸到他脖子上那条「围脖」，手便停住了，一动也不动，好像生怕一动，便会把什么东西惊醒了。

然后她把手收回去，朝着那团谁都看不见的银光，很慢、很慢地低下了头，低得几乎到了膝盖上，又慢慢地抬起来，脸上什么表情也没有。

「回罢。日头上来了，马家的人，也该到了。」
story.en:
At the house at the east end, Granny Wu was already sitting on her threshold, face turned east, where the first fish-belly white was just showing; it was probably that strip of white she was sunning in.

Xiaoman came up to her, and before he spoke she said, "The venison's come?"

Xiaoman stood with the crock on his back, stunned. His mother hadn't said a word about a deer leg. He said, "…How do you know it's a deer leg?"

Granny Wu said, "Your father promised. By the mountain stream, crouched there feeling the hoofprint."

Xiaoman's heart gave a jolt. That stream was inside Black Pine Ridge, thirty or forty li from this threshold at least. "Granny, you weren't by the stream."

Granny Wu laughed, showing her three teeth. "My ears are good."

She lifted the lid of the crock and sniffed. "Your mother is a clever woman." She patted the threshold. "Sit."

So Xiaoman sat. Granny Wu asked, "Your grandpa's bow — you drew it yesterday?" Xiaoman was taken aback. "…I drew it." Granny Wu nodded, lifted her face toward that strip of white in the east, and slowly told a story.

Long ago, the very first emperor under heaven took copper from the mountain and cast a *ding* at a mountain's foot. The day it was cast, a dragon came down from the sky and let its whiskers down to fetch him. The emperor climbed on; his great officers and consorts climbed up after him, seventy-odd of them, and the dragon flew up toward heaven.

The ones left were small officials, too small to squeeze on. One of them lived right at the foot of that mountain and had a daughter, seven or eight years old. He threw himself at the dragon's whiskers and clung there, hanging in mid-air, and below him his daughter turned up her face and called him, again and again. The whiskers tore; the people all fell; and down with them fell the emperor's bow.

Xiaoman said, "And the daughter?" Granny Wu said, "…Cried, what else."

She paused, then went on: "The common folk looked up, hugging that bow, and wept. Later people called that place Dinghu, and that bow, Wuhao. Those who went up went up; those left behind kept a bow."

Xiaoman asked: "That bow — did anyone ever draw it after?"

Granny Wu turned her face to him, and slowly a smile came. "You ask well."

She went no further, only added, half to herself: "Cultivating immortality, cultivating immortality — if what you've cultivated is a man who wants to go up to heaven, that's as far as it goes."

When she'd finished, she reached out her bony hand to touch his head, found the "scarf" round his neck, and there her hand stopped, not moving at all, as though afraid that any movement would wake something.

Then she drew her hand back and, toward that silver light nobody could see, very, very slowly bowed her head, nearly to her knees; then slowly straightened, her face showing nothing.

"Go home. The sun's up; the Mas will be on their way."

label.en: Stay in and watch over it

exits.means: stays home with the fox that night

story.zh:
那缸腌菜，是他爹送去的。他爹瘸着腿去了，瘸着腿回来，说吴婆婆接了缸，揭开盖子闻了闻，什么也没说，只朝着他们家这边，坐了好一会儿。

小满没出门。他守着怀里那团凉冰冰的银毛，数了三遍它还在不在喘气。日头上来了，马家的人，也该到了。
story.en:
It was his father who took the crock over. He limped there and limped back, and said Granny Wu took the crock, lifted the lid and sniffed, and said not a word, only sat facing their house for a good while.

Xiaoman stayed in. He watched over the cold silver fur inside his jacket, and three times counted whether it was still breathing. The sun was up; the Mas would be coming.
